key_insight: VLM-IE3D improves vision-language models by giving them a stronger sense of 3D space, using both implicit and explicit geometry learned from RGB videos. This helps the model reason better about spatial relationships and 3D tasks than standard 2D-only VLMs.
problem_solved: Most vision-language models are trained on 2D images and struggle with tasks that require accurate 3D spatial understanding, such as depth, layout, and object relations in space.
method: Introduces Implicit Geometry Tokens (IGTs) to encode high-level geometric priors from video data.
Adds explicit 3D geometry representations to make spatial structure easier for the model to use.
Combines both geometry types in a unified framework to strengthen 3D reasoning in VLMs.
impact: This matters because many real-world AI applications depend on understanding the physical world in 3D, not just recognizing objects in 2D. Practitioners building robotics, AR/VR, embodied AI, or spatial assistants can benefit from VLMs that reason more reliably about geometry.

paper_title: 3D-Aware VLMs with Implicit and Explicit Geometries
paper_authors: Wenhao Li, Xueying Jiang, Quanhao Qian, Deli Zhao, Ran Xu
